Command: A Nazirite shall shave and bring offerings when the vow ends
Summary: When the days of the Nazirite vow are fulfilled, the Nazirite shaves the head of his separation at the door of the tabernacle and brings a burnt offering, a sin offering, and a peace offering.
Commandment: When the vow is fulfilled, the Nazirite shall shave his head at the door of the tabernacle and bring the offerings of completion.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Acts 21:23-26 shows Paul joining men under a vow in Jerusalem, which shows the practice continued among Jewish believers, not that it is imposed on Christians.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the Nazirite separates himself unto the LORD (Numbers 6:2,5-6); no further reason is given, so the components' purposes are traditional — wine abstained from as a mark of consecration, hair uncut as the visible sign, and corpse-avoidance as the priest-like holiness of the vow; the closing shaving and offerings return the separated one to ordinary life.
